_comment: SAP ABAP Harness — .mcp.json stamped by /scaffold-abap. Wires ONLY the sap-adt bridge (node mcp-adt-bridge/server.js), the single external substrate: the MCP-ADT server exposing the aws_abap_cb_* tools. MOCK MODE = fully offline: run the ADT sidecar with S4_TRIAL_URL unset and no live SAP is contacted — every aws_abap_cb_* call is served from the sidecar's mock fixtures, so /scaffold-abap and the read/plan lanes work with zero SAP connectivity. Point ADT_MCP_URL at a live sidecar (S4_TRIAL_URL set) only when you intend real ADT reads. Writes are fail-closed by default (P5): HARNESS_ADT_ALLOW_WRITE="0" makes every write tool refuse; a human sets it to "1" on a non-prod tier and still releases the transport by hand.

sap-adt._comment_env: ADT_MCP_URL — URL of the MCP-ADT sidecar (default http://127.0.0.1:8090, loopback only). HARNESS_ADT_ALLOW_WRITE — write gate, default "0" = writes fail closed (P5, non-prod-only, human releases the transport). Set "1" ONLY against a non-production tier; never in a shared or prod context.

mcpServers._comment_optional_servers: The sap-adt bridge is the default substrate this template wires. The full harness also ships two OFFLINE servers you can add here when the project needs them: abap-analyser ("command": "node", "args": ["analyser/server.js"]) — @abaplint/core code property graph + S/4 readiness; and greenfield ("command": "node", "args": ["greenfield/server.js"]) — released-API grounding + ABAP-Cloud linter. Add a server explicitly, enable it deliberately, and settle .mcp.json before any long /abap-auto run (P7 — editing it mid-run busts the prompt cache).
